opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048) is a full-time Engineer. Requested admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted per policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kim Dunn (E048) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractor policy: read max (write requires advanced training; admin never). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Conflicting evidence: HR note lists Kim Dunn as full-time Engineer (which would allow admin on Source Code), while the Security DB note lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never permitted). Given the conflict, I apply the more restrictive policy. As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed level is read, and the requested admin exceeds it, so grant read.

Actually, let me reconsider. The notes: Note 1 is presumably from HR agent (employment type full_time, role Engineer). Note 2 from Security agent (contractor, basic training). The Security DB shows contractor. HR says full-time. Contradiction.
